questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Canon at the unison and canon at an interval
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish unison canon from interval canon
questions.stem: In my beekeeper logbook entry of March 3 I note a canon whose voices enter at the same pitch.

options.text: That is a canon at the unison.
That is a canon at the fifth.
That is a canon at the octave.

questions.explanation: Voices entering at the same pitch form a canon at the unison. Interval canons transpose the following voice.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting the overlap in a stretto
questions.stem: My April 5 log counts a stretto where the second voice enters two measures into a five-measure subject.
questions.explanation: Five measures minus two measures of entry offset leaves three measures of overlap. The subtraction gives the overlap length.
questions.hint: Subtract entry offset from subject length.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: How a fugue reaches its final cadence
questions.stem: On May 7 my logbook records how a fugue closes with a perfect authentic cadence.

answer.exemplar: A fugue typically closes with a perfect authentic cadence in the tonic, often after a final statement of the subject in the tonic key.

questions.explanation: The closing cadence is usually a perfect authentic cadence in the tonic. A deceptive cadence would not close firmly.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
